findings.text: Slow-clock control packs four single-bit power signals in the low half and a divider in the upper half. The bits request forced slow operation, control whether power logic honors core PLL-off requests, enable crystal shutdown management, and report crystal running as read-only, with values 0x800, 0x1000, 0x2000 and 0x4000; the divider mask is 0xFFFF0000 with shift 16 and slow rate described as one over four plus divisor. System clock control identified as SSB_CHIPCO_SYSCLKCTL at 0xC0, noted for revision three and later, offers idle-power enable, active-power enable, forced PLL on, forced active-power and forced high-throughput requests at 0x1, 0x2, 0x4, 0x8 and 0x10, plus a high-half divider 0xFFFF0000 shift 16 for the low-power clock, with status word SSB_CHIPCO_CLKSTSTR at 0xC4.

External-memory configuration uses a stepped block from 0x100: PCMCIA config plus memory, attribute and I/O waits at 0x100 through 0x10C, IDE config plus three waits at 0x110 through 0x11C, programmable config plus wait count at 0x120 and 0x124, and flash config plus wait count at 0x128 and 0x12C. Clock word SSB_CHIPCO_CLKCTLST for newer revisions at 0x1E0 carries low-byte requests for forced active clock, forced high-throughput, forced idle, availability requests and hardware-off override at 0x1, 0x2, 0x4, 0x8, 0x10 and 0x20, with availability indications at 0x10000 and 0x20000; a workaround word follows at 0x1E4. Two serial blocks with bases SSB_CHIPCO_UART0_DATA at 0x300 and SSB_CHIPCO_UART1_DATA at 0x400 each step four bytes through data, interrupt mask, FIFO, line, modem, line status, modem status and scratch.

Registers from SSB_CHIPCO_PMU_CTL through SSB_CHIPCO_PLLCTL_DATA occupy 0x600 upward with four-byte spacing except for a gap before request timers: control 0x600, capability 0x604, status 0x608, resource status 0x60C, pending 0x610, timer 0x614, minimum mask 0x618, maximum mask 0x61C, table select 0x620, dependency mask 0x624, up-down timer 0x628, resource timer 0x62C, stretch 0x630, watchdog 0x634, request-timer select 0x640, request timer 0x644 and request mask 0x648, then address and data pairs for chip control 0x650 and 0x654, register control 0x658 and 0x65C, and PLL control 0x660 and 0x664. Control blends low-power oscillator select 0x1, divider enable 0x2, crystal-frequency field 0x7C shift 2, active and high-throughput request enables 0x80 and 0x100, no-idle-on-wait 0x200, PLL update 0x400 and high-half divider 0xFFFF0000 shift 16. Status reports resource-init 0x3, availability 0x4 and 0x8, backplane state 0x30 and pending interrupt 0x40; capability revision mask is 0xFF.

Type-zero PLL programming uses indices SSB_PMU0_PLLCTL0 through SSB_PMU0_PLLCTL2 reached through the PLL address and data pair. Index zero carries a single-bit predivider mask 0x1 with associated reference frequency 25000 kilohertz. Index one combines a low-nibble integer mask in the top nibble 0xF0000000 shift 28, a fractional mask 0xFFFFF00 shift 8, and a stop-modulation flag 0x40. Index two holds the complementary high nibble of the integer field as 0xF shift zero, so the integer contribution spans two registers.

Type-one PLL programming uses indices SSB_PMU1_PLLCTL0 through SSB_PMU1_PLLCTL5. Index zero holds predivider nibbles 0xF00000 shift 20 and 0xF000000 shift 24. Index one packs multiplier bytes 0xFF, 0xFF00, 0xFF0000 and 0xFF000000 at shifts zero, eight, sixteen and twenty-four. Index two combines bytes 0xFF and 0xFF00 at shifts zero and eight with mode 0xE0000 shift 17 and integer 0x1FF00000 shift 20. Index three is fractional 0xFFFFFF shift zero, index four has no documented subfields, and index five carries drive field 0xFFFFFF00 shift eight.

Resource numbering from SSB_PMURES_4312_SWITCHER_BURST through SSB_PMURES_4312_HT_AVAIL assigns integers zero through fourteen in bring-up order, advancing by one per listed resource: switcher burst and pulse modes, reference and core-burst and core-pulse and radio regulators, idle request, bandgap and transmit and receive filter bypasses, crystal power-up, active-clock availability, baseband and radio PLL bypasses, and high-throughput availability last. Values denote ordinal positions for mask and table programming rather than bit masks.

Resource numbering from SSB_PMURES_4325_BUCK_BOOST_BURST through SSB_PMURES_4325_HT_AVAIL spans zero through twenty-one advancing by one: buck-boost burst, current-buck burst and pulse modes, core regulator over buck burst and pulse modes, buck-boost pulse mode, idle request, analog-buck burst and pulse modes, four low-noise regulator power-ups, crystal power, active availability, six power-switch enables for receive, transmit, radio PLL, local oscillator, analog front end and baseband PLL, and high-throughput availability last. Idle request is six, crystal power thirteen and active availability fourteen.

Resource numberings from SSB_PMURES_4328_EXT_SWITCHER_PWM through SSB_PMURES_4328_BB_PLL_PU and from SSB_PMURES_5354_EXT_SWITCHER_PWM through SSB_PMURES_5354_BB_PLL_PU share an identical twenty-entry order zero through nineteen advancing by one: external switcher pulse mode, baseband switcher pulse mode, baseband switcher burst, baseband external switcher burst, idle request, radio switcher pulse mode and burst, ROM switch, reference and radio and analog and PLL regulators, bandgap and transmit and receive bypasses, crystal power-up and enable, baseband and radio PLL bypasses, and baseband PLL power-up last. Ordinals match across the two families though symbol prefixes differ.

Chip-status words encode storage selection and calibration in low bits. One part uses a single present flag SSB_CHIPCO_CHST_4322_SPROM_EXISTS at 0x40. The 4325 family multiplexes two low bits under mask 0x3 with values zero through three meaning default configuration with no storage, storage present with OTP powered, OTP only with no storage, and OTP powered down with storage present. The same word carries mode flag 0x4 shift two, calibration-valid flag 0x8 shift three, five-bit calibration value 0x1F0 shift four, and topology flag 0x200 distinguishing two minor variants.

Storage-presence tests are pure functions of the status word. The 4312 test reports present unless the two-bit selector equals the OTP-only value. The 4322 test reports present when the dedicated single-bit flag is set. The 4325 test reports present only when the selector equals neither the default-configuration value nor the OTP-only value, so two of four selector states mean absent and the other two mean present. No other status bits affect these three predicates.

N and M clock words expose packed divider controls. The N word places six-bit N1 at 0x3F, N2 at 0x3F00 shift eight, and PLL control nibble at 0xF0000 shift sixteen. The M word places M1 at 0x3F, M2 at 0x3F00 shift eight, M3 at 0x3F0000 shift sixteen, and five-bit mux selector at 0x1F000000 shift twenty-four. Each shift aligns its mask to the least significant bit, so software extracts a field by masking then right-shifting.

Clock-factor encodings use sparse constants: six-bit factors for two through seven are 0x2, 0x3, 0x5, 0x9, 0x11 and 0x21, five-bit fields add bias five, type-two N1 N2 M1 M3 add bias two while M2 adds bias three, and type-two mux bypasses are 1, 2 and 4. Mux combinations are bypass 0x8, M1 0x4, M1-M2 0x2, M1-M2-M3 0x1 and M1-M3 0x11. Type-six mask is 1 with backplane rates 120000000 and 100000000 for values zero and one and MIPS rate twice backplane. Base frequencies are 24000000 and 12500000, and the 5350 part fixes N at 0x311 and M at 0x4020009.

External-interface configuration packs enable, mode, width and synchronous controls into one word. Enable is 0x1, mode mask is 0xE with asynchronous parallel flash at 0x2, synchronous at 0x4, PCMCIA at 0x8 and IDE at 0xA, data width selects eight versus sixteen bits at 0x10, synchronous divisor occupies 0x60, synchronous clock enable is 0x80, and size or bytestrobe is 0x100. Mode values overlap bit patterns so IDE shares bits with other modes and must be decoded as a whole field rather than as independent flags.

Serial-flash control defines twelve operation codes combining transfer length and opcode: write enable 0x6, write disable 0x4, read status 0x105, write status 0x101, read data 0x303, page program 0x302, sector erase 0x2D8, bulk erase 0xC7, deep power-down 0xB9, signature read 0x3AB, keep-select 0x1000 and sub-sector erase 0x220. Status reports write-in-progress 0x1, write-enable latch 0x2, three-bit block protection 0x1C shift two, and register-write disable 0x80. Upper bits of operation codes encode length while the low byte carries the flash opcode.

Clock readiness follows a three-level progression from idle low-power through active to high-throughput. Software issues force or request signals for each level and hardware answers with availability indications; higher levels imply lower ones are usable, and power logic may manage transitions autonomously unless forced. System control, newer clock control and PMU status domains all expose parallel available flags while control words expose matching force and enable bits, so drivers poll availability after requesting and must not assume immediate readiness.

Early variant 4328A0 reverses availability indications in the newer clock control word, swapping active-clock and high-throughput positions relative to all other parts, documented by distinct masks SSB_CHIPCO_CLKCTLST_4328A0_HAVEHT and SSB_CHIPCO_CLKCTLST_4328A0_HAVEALP alongside the normal masks. Code testing availability with standard masks will misread readiness on that variant, possibly waiting for the wrong level or proceeding before the required clock is stable.
